title: Why Cold Showers Are Good for You and the Planet
paragraphs: Starting or ending the day under a frosty shower might not be everyone's favorite thing. But it could have benefits for both your health and the environment.

Researchers from the University of Basel in Switzerland looked at over 700 people aged 18 to 65. Some of these people took 30- to 120-second cold showers for 12 weeks. The others — the control group — took showers as usual.
All the participants were in good health, and weren't already in the habit of taking cold showers.
They regularly reported on how their showers were going, and also reported on their health, including whether they'd taken days off work due to illness.
Not everyone was able to stick to cold showers, however. But the researchers continued to count anyone who took cold showers at least 70% of the time as part of the cold shower group.

And it was found that the cold shower group took 31% fewer days off for illness compared to the control group. The cold shower group also got significantly better scores on tests of their psychological well-being.

The researchers weren't just interested in the health effects of cold showers. They also noted that people spend less time in the shower when the water is cold, which reduces their water consumption — a boon for the planet and their water bill!
Cold showers also reduce energy consumption. The researchers estimated that each cold shower saved enough energy to power an average refrigerator for almost four hours.

While cold showers may be good for health and the environment, researcher Lena Glaser says people don't need to force themselves under icy water — because any decrease in temperature should have benefits.
"The water doesn't have to be equally cold every day," she said. "We don't feel equally brave every day, and that's okay."
She also noted that participants seemed to gradually get used to cold showers as they continued to take them regularly.
